reasons: The rule targets post-termination data return and transition assistance; the cited exit provisions (Sections 11.3 and 5.3) contain only a 'return or destroy' obligation for Confidential Information at the other party's election, with no obligation to return Corio's or its Customers' hosted data, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification — so the clause fails the fallback ('data export within 30 days') on a material term, making the deviation/insert classification correct rather than over-flagging.

The redline is a pure insert (new Section 11.4) appended to the termination-effects section, leaving all existing language untouched — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it tracks the model language with party names correctly mapped (Commerce One as Vendor, Corio as Customer).

The added legal-retention carve-out and 'at Corio's request' triggers are reasonable, do not weaken our position, and keep the deletion obligation from colliding with Commerce One's surviving post-termination support obligations to then-existing Software Users.

The comment is accurate on what Section 11.3 does and does not do, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback; tone, prefix and first-person plural are compliant.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and that data return/transition language is present in the result.
